content: [{"id": "t0", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "HD Setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Everything the helpdesk reads when a ticket is raised, classified and moved. Values are curated here; nothing is enforced until it is configured.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t2", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How a ticket is classified", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Types. The broad reason a ticket exists, curated in Ticket Types. Renaming a type carries every ticket with it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Sub types. The specific problem, curated in Ticket Sub Types. Each one declares the type it belongs to, and a ticket is refused a sub type of any other type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Sources. Where the ticket started, curated in Ticket Sources: phone, email, WhatsApp or anything else. Routing says which team a mailbox's tickets belong to, and helpdesk's own rotation assigns them from there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Put them on the agent's screen. A field is offered to an agent only when the ticket template lists it, in Ticket Templates.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A value is retired by ticking Disabled, never by deleting it: it stops being offered while every ticket that already carries it is left untouched.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t8", "type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}}, {"id": "t9", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How a ticket moves", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t10", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Statuses. The states a ticket can be in, curated in Ticket Statuses. Each one is categorised Open, Paused or Resolved, and that category is what pauses the service clock.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t11", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Allowed moves. One row per move in Ticket Transitions: from which status, to which status, which role may make it, and which fields must be filled first, such as the internal team a ticket waits on or the reason it was resolved. A move with no row is refused.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t12", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Finality. A status with no rows leading out of it cannot be left, which is how a resolved ticket is made final.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t13", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "While Ticket Transitions holds no rows, tickets move exactly as they do today. The first row switches the rule on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t14", "type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}}, {"id": "card1", "type": "card", "data": {"card_name": "Classification", "col": 4}}, {"id": "card2", "type": "card", "data": {"card_name": "Lifecycle", "col": 4}}, {"id": "card3", "type": "card", "data": {"card_name": "Screen and people", "col": 4}}, {"id": "t29", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Tickets", "col": 4}}]
